weeks.outcome: Build, debug, explain, and verify a labelled arithmetic program.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse compiler, main, header, variable type, printf format so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a labelled arithmetic program.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 1 Skill Check, then preview the a labelled arithmetic program contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: Compile, Run, and Basic Values Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines compiler. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: translates C source into a program
the representation and operations of a value

questions.explanation: compiler means translates C source into a program; it is used to run gcc source.c -o app. Avoid this mistake: expect source to execute without compilation.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to run gcc source.c -o app. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: compiler is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect source to execute without compilation.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for main, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: print every type with the same format specifier

questions.explanation: main means the program entry function; it is used to return 0 from main. Avoid this mistake: write executable statements outside functions.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to write executable statements outside functions. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: main is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to write executable statements outside functions.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates header?
questions.explanation: header means declarations included before use; it is used to include stdio.h for printf. Avoid this mistake: paste library implementation into source.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: include stdio.h for printf?
questions.explanation: header is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to paste library implementation into source.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain variable type before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: the representation and operations of a value
a placeholder matching an argument type
translates C source into a program

questions.explanation: variable type means the representation and operations of a value; it is used to use int for counts. Avoid this mistake: print every type with the same format specifier.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "the representation and operations of a value". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: variable type is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to print every type with the same format specifier.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that printf format was misunderstood?

options.label: expect source to execute without compilation

questions.explanation: printf format means a placeholder matching an argument type; it is used to use %d for int. Avoid this mistake: supply fewer arguments than placeholders.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—supply fewer arguments than placeholders—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: printf format is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to supply fewer arguments than placeholders.

builds.title: Microbuild: a labelled arithmetic program
builds.outcome: A working, tested a labelled arithmetic program.
builds.brief: Deliverable: a labelled arithmetic program. Required behavior: demonstrate compiler, main, header, variable type, printf format; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a labelled arithmetic program: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make compiler, main, header visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using variable type and printf format. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—supply fewer arguments than placeholders—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a labelled arithmetic program through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 1 concepts: compiler, main, header, variable type, printf format.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving compiler and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "supply fewer arguments than placeholders" and change one cause at a time.

questions.prompt: The Week 2 guide defines scanf result. Which description matches that definition?

questions.prompt: The learner needs to check scanf returns 1. Which concept from the Week 2 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: scanf result is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to assume invalid input changed the variable.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for address operator, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: use & with an array name in basic string input

questions.explanation: address operator means produces an object address; it is used to pass &count to scanf. Avoid this mistake: use & with an array name in basic string input.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to use & with an array name in basic string input. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: address operator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use & with an array name in basic string input.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 2 guide correctly demonstrates integer division?
questions.explanation: integer division means whole-number division for int operands; it is used to 7 / 2 produces 3. Avoid this mistake: expect 3.5 without a floating operand.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: 7 / 2 produces 3?
questions.explanation: integer division is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect 3.5 without a floating operand.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain if statement before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: the number of successfully read fields

questions.explanation: if statement means conditional execution; it is used to reject division by zero. Avoid this mistake: use = where == is required.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "conditional execution". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: if statement is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use = where == is required.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that logical operator was misunderstood?

options.label: assume invalid input changed the variable

questions.explanation: logical operator means combines boolean-like expressions; it is used to check choice >= 1 && choice <= 4. Avoid this mistake: confuse bitwise & with logical &&.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—confuse bitwise & with logical &&—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: logical operator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to confuse bitwise & with logical &&.

skillCheck.title: Compile, Run, and Basic Values Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines compiler. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: translates C source into a program
the representation and operations of a value

questions.explanation: compiler means translates C source into a program; it is used to run gcc source.c -o app. Avoid this mistake: expect source to execute without compilation.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to run gcc source.c -o app. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: compiler is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect source to execute without compilation.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for main, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: print every type with the same format specifier

questions.explanation: main means the program entry function; it is used to return 0 from main. Avoid this mistake: write executable statements outside functions.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to write executable statements outside functions. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: main is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to write executable statements outside functions.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates header?
questions.explanation: header means declarations included before use; it is used to include stdio.h for printf. Avoid this mistake: paste library implementation into source.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: include stdio.h for printf?
questions.explanation: header is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to paste library implementation into source.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain variable type before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: the representation and operations of a value
a placeholder matching an argument type
translates C source into a program

questions.explanation: variable type means the representation and operations of a value; it is used to use int for counts. Avoid this mistake: print every type with the same format specifier.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "the representation and operations of a value". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: variable type is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to print every type with the same format specifier.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that printf format was misunderstood?

options.label: expect source to execute without compilation

questions.explanation: printf format means a placeholder matching an argument type; it is used to use %d for int. Avoid this mistake: supply fewer arguments than placeholders.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—supply fewer arguments than placeholders—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: printf format is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to supply fewer arguments than placeholders.
